_about: Quizzes written here replace a lesson's Ghost quiz. Types: choice (choices + answer index), blank (q with ____, words, answer), order (items in the right order), match (pairs). Every question has a why. draft: true means not reviewed yet.

questions.q: Byzantine worship grew from the way Christians prayed in Antioch.
questions.why: True! The Catholic Encyclopedia says it “is derived from that of Antioch.”

questions.q: What do Byzantine Catholics and Roman Catholics share?
questions.why: We share one faith and the same seven sacraments. We just pray in different ways (CCC 1202).

questions.q: “It was in ____ that the disciples were first called Christians.”
questions.why: Acts 11:26. Christians got their name in the city of Antioch.

questions.q: The Catholic Church is only the Roman, or Latin, Church.
questions.why: False! The Catholic Church is a family of Churches, Eastern and Western (Christ – Our Pascha 285).

questions.q: Who are all the Catholic Churches united with?
choices: The Pope, who takes Saint Peter’s place
questions.why: All the Catholic Churches are united with the Pope, “the successor of the apostle Peter” (Christ – Our Pascha 291).

questions.q: Where does the word “Byzantine” come from?
choices: The city of Byzantium, named for Byzas
questions.why: The city was “naturally called Byzantion” after Byzas, its founder.

questions.q: “Byzantine” is a way of praying that many different peoples share.
questions.why: True! Greeks, Slavs, Arabs and others pray the Byzantine liturgy, which spread from Constantinople.

questions.q: Byzantium was renamed ____, after Emperor Constantine.
questions.why: Constantine made it his capital, and the city took his name: Constantinople.

questions.q: What did Byzantine Catholics keep?
choices: Their Byzantine prayers, and unity with Rome
questions.why: They kept their Byzantine way of praying and stayed in communion with the Church of Rome.

questions.q: Byzantine Catholics and Orthodox Christians pray the same Byzantine liturgy.
questions.why: True! The difference is unity with the Pope. The Catechism says our communion “lacks little to attain the fullness” (CCC 838).

questions.q: What is the wall of icons called?
questions.why: The iconostasis is a wall of icons that separates and unites the sanctuary and the nave.

questions.q: In an icon of Mary, she points us to Jesus.
questions.why: True! The Mother of God holds Christ and points to him, showing us the way.

questions.q: The doors in the middle of the iconostasis are called the ____ Doors.
questions.why: The Royal (or Holy) Doors are in the center of the iconostasis.

questions.q: How do Byzantine Catholics receive Holy Communion?
choices: From a cup they hold themselves
questions.why: The priest gives the Body and Blood of Christ with a spoon, for the cleansing from sins.

questions.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
questions.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

questions.q: Match each one to what it is.
questions.why: Byzantine churches have a wall of icons called an iconostasis, with the Royal Doors in the middle, and Communion is given with a golden spoon.

questions.q: Why do we make the Sign of the Cross?
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: the Christian “professes faith in the Most Holy Trinity.”

questions.q: Which shoulder do Byzantine Catholics touch first?
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the right shoulder to the left.”

questions.q: Three fingers joined stand for the Holy ____.
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: joining the first three fingers is “a sign of our profession of faith in the Holy Trinity.”

questions.q: The Church holds all lawfully recognized rites to be of equal right and dignity.
questions.why: True! Catechism 1203: all lawful rites are “of equal right and dignity.”

questions.q: Put the Byzantine Sign of the Cross in order.
questions.why: Christ – Our Pascha 626: “from the forehead to the breast and from the right shoulder to the left.”

questions.q: What job did Jesus give Peter?
questions.why: Luke 22:32: “you must strengthen your brothers.”

questions.q: Infallibility means the Pope always knows who will win the big game.
questions.why: False! Catechism 891: the gift is for “a doctrine pertaining to faith or morals.”

questions.q: Infallible means can't be ____.
questions.why: Infallible means unable to be wrong. Catechism 889: Jesus gave his Church “a share in his own infallibility.”

questions.q: The Pope never makes any mistakes at all.
questions.why: False! The Catholic Encyclopedia says infallibility “is not attributed to every doctrinal act of the pope.”

questions.q: What is Lent?
questions.why: In the video: Lent is the 40 days before Easter, when Catholics pray, fast and prepare.

questions.q: Lent starts on Ash ____.
questions.why: In the video: that is why Catholics start the Lenten season with Ash Wednesday.

questions.q: On the Fridays of Lent, Catholics don't eat…
questions.why: In the video: every Friday of Lent, Catholics abstain from meat and eat fish instead.

questions.q: The number 40 in the Bible. Match each one.
pairs: 40 days on the mountain with God
questions.why: In the video: it rained 40 days in the flood, Moses was on the mountain 40 days, and Jesus fasted 40 days in the desert.

questions.q: How many Stations of the Cross are there?
questions.why: In the video: there have traditionally been 14 stations.

questions.q: The Stations of the Cross follow the path Jesus walked to be ____.
questions.why: In the video: it is believed to be the actual path that Jesus walked when he was crucified.

questions.q: Put these stations in order.
questions.why: In the video: 1, Jesus is condemned. 2, he carries his cross. 4, he meets his mother. 12, Jesus dies on the cross.

questions.q: Who helps Jesus carry the cross?
questions.why: In the video: station 5, Simon of Cyrene helps Jesus carry the cross.

questions.q: Why are there people who do bad things in the Church?
questions.why: In the video: the Church is made of humans, and people are flawed. They make mistakes.

questions.q: Can a priest who sins still forgive sins in confession?
questions.why: In the video: he can, because it is not by his power that he gives the sacraments, but by Jesus Christ's power.

questions.q: Peter denied Jesus three times, but Jesus still made him the first ____.
questions.why: In the video: Jesus still made Peter the first Pope.

questions.q: What should we do for people who do wrong?
questions.why: In the video: it's not our job to point fingers and judge, but to pray for them and help them on their way to heaven.

questions.q: Why do churches have beautiful art?
choices: To remind us of the beauty of heaven
questions.why: In the video: churches should have beautiful art to remind us of the beauty of heaven.

questions.q: Who should sacred art show?
questions.why: In the video: religious art should include Christ, the Virgin Mary, or one of the saints.

questions.q: Long ago, many people couldn't ____, so pictures taught them the faith.
questions.why: In the video: when not many people could read, sacred art was a great way to learn and understand the faith.

questions.q: Which of these was a great artist the Church supported?
questions.why: In the video: the Church has always supported artists such as Michelangelo, Da Vinci and Caravaggio.

questions.q: When do we genuflect (bend the right knee)?
choices: Passing in front of the tabernacle
At the end of a song
questions.why: In the video: we genuflect any time we pass in front of a tabernacle that holds the Blessed Sacrament.

questions.q: Bending the knee is a sign of ____ for Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament.
questions.why: In the video: a genuflection signifies adoration, so it is reserved for the Most Blessed Sacrament.

questions.q: At which name do we bow our heads?
questions.why: In the video: “at the name of Jesus every knee should bend.” We bow our heads at the name of Jesus.

questions.q: Match each one to what we do.
questions.why: In the video: we genuflect when we pass the tabernacle, and bow our heads at the name of Jesus, Mary, and the Trinity.

questions.q: On which days do Catholics go to Mass?
questions.why: In the video: we are obliged to attend Mass every Sunday and Holy Day of Obligation.

questions.q: Which is a good reason to stay home from Mass?
questions.why: In the video: a serious illness, like anything contagious or anything that keeps you from leaving the house.

questions.q: If you are sick, staying home protects the other ____.
questions.why: In the video: people who love Mass should still think of the other parishioners when they're sick.

questions.q: Who else might stay home with a sick little child?
questions.why: In the video: when young children get sick, parents have to care for them and may miss Mass.

questions.q: Holy Week begins on ____ Sunday.
questions.why: In the video: Holy Week begins on Palm Sunday.

questions.q: Put the days of Holy Week in order.
questions.why: In the video: Holy Week begins on Palm Sunday, then Holy Thursday, Good Friday and Holy Saturday, before Easter.

questions.q: Match each day to what it remembers.
questions.why: In the video: Holy Thursday remembers the Eucharist, Good Friday Christ's passion and death, and Holy Saturday his burial.

questions.q: On Holy Thursday, whose feet did Jesus wash?
questions.why: In the video: the washing of the feet remembers Christ washing the feet of the apostles at the Last Supper.

questions.q: When is Epiphany?
questions.why: In the video: Epiphany is celebrated on January 6th, 12 days after Christmas.

questions.q: Who visited baby Jesus at Epiphany?
questions.why: In the video: the first event is when the three wise men, or kings, visited the infant Jesus.

questions.q: Epiphany also remembers when John the Baptist ____ Jesus.
questions.why: In the video: the second event was when Saint John the Baptist baptized Jesus.

questions.q: In many Latin American countries, who brings gifts to children?
questions.why: In the video: in many Latin American countries, it is the three wise men, not Santa Claus, who bring gifts.

questions.q: What is the Golden Rule?
choices: Treat others the way you'd like to be treated
questions.why: In the video: the Golden Rule is to treat others the way you'd like to be treated.

questions.q: Match what you like to what you should do.
pairs: You like it when others share
You like a smile and “good morning”
questions.why: In the video: if you like it when people share, share your toys. If you like a smile, smile at others. If you don't like mean words, don't say them.

questions.q: If someone doesn't follow the Golden Rule, should you give up on it?
questions.why: In the video: you should not give up on the Golden Rule, because most of the time it works.

questions.q: The Golden Rule is worth more than ____.
questions.why: In the video: the Golden Rule is very valuable, much more valuable than gold.

questions.q: Saint Aidan was a monk from which country?
questions.why: In the video: Aidan was an Irish monk and missionary.

questions.q: Aidan founded a monastery on the island of ____.
questions.why: In the video: he founded a monastic cathedral on the island of Lindisfarne, and was its first bishop.

questions.q: How did Aidan share the Gospel?
choices: He walked from village to village talking with people
questions.why: In the video: Aidan walked from one village to another, kindly talking with the people and caring about their lives.

questions.q: Who did Saint Aidan especially help?
questions.why: In the video: he gave orphans a home and schooling, and used his own gifts to pay for the freedom of slaves.

questions.q: On Ash Wednesday, what shape does the priest make with ashes on our forehead?
questions.why: In the video: the priest puts ashes in the shape of a cross on our forehead.

questions.q: The ashes come from burning the ____ from last year's Palm Sunday.
questions.why: In the video: the ashes come from burning the palms that were blessed on Palm Sunday the year before.

questions.q: What do the ashes remind us?
questions.why: In the video: we are all made from dust, and one day we will return to dust.

questions.q: Ash Wednesday starts which time of the year?
questions.why: In the video: Ash Wednesday is a special day in the time of year called Lent.

questions.q: What is penance?
choices: Showing we're sorry for sin with our actions
questions.why: In the video: penance is saying I'm sorry with your actions.

questions.q: What is mortification?
choices: Giving something up to root out a bad habit
questions.why: In the video: mortification is giving up something harmless to build strength against a bad habit.

questions.q: Match each word to what it means.
pairs: Giving up a habit to grow stronger
questions.why: In the video: penance says I'm sorry; mortification roots out the bad habit so we don't fall again.

questions.q: Penance is like buying ____ after forgetting someone's birthday.
questions.why: In the video: penance is like buying flowers after forgetting someone's birthday.

questions.q: What do we do first, to know what we're sorry for?
questions.why: In the video: start with an examination of conscience, going through the Ten Commandments.

questions.q: Who gives us a penance in confession?
questions.why: In the video: go to confession and the priest gives you a proper penance.

questions.q: Which one is a good penance?
questions.why: In the video: common penances are the Our Father, three Hail Marys, the Stations of the Cross, the Rosary, and reading the Gospels.

questions.q: Put these in order.
questions.why: In the video: first examine your conscience, then go to confession, and the priest gives you a penance to do.

questions.q: Which Sunday of Lent is Laetare Sunday?
questions.why: In the video: Laetare Sunday is the fourth Sunday of Lent.

questions.q: “Laetare” means ____!
questions.why: In the video: Laetare Jerusalem means rejoice, O Jerusalem.

questions.q: What color can the priest wear on Laetare Sunday?
questions.why: In the video: rose-colored vestments instead of purple, with flowers on the altar and the organ playing.

questions.q: How long is Lent?
questions.why: In the video: Lent starts about six weeks before Easter and lasts for 40 days.

questions.q: In the last two weeks of Lent, what covers statues and crosses?
questions.why: In the video: crosses, statues and pictures are covered with a violet veil.

questions.q: Why are they covered?
choices: Jesus no longer walked openly, but hid himself
questions.why: In the video: during this time Christ no longer walked openly among the people, but hid himself.

questions.q: Passiontide starts on ____ Sunday.
questions.why: In the video: these are the two weeks between Passion Sunday and Easter.

questions.q: Palm Sunday begins which week?
questions.why: In the video: Palm Sunday is the beginning of Holy Week.

questions.q: What do we remember with the palm branches?
questions.why: In the video: we remember the day Jesus entered Jerusalem and the people welcomed him by waving palm branches.

questions.q: Put Palm Sunday in order.
questions.why: In the video: the priest blesses the palms, they're carried in a procession, and then Mass is celebrated.

questions.q: Old palms are burned to make the ashes for Ash ____.
questions.why: In the video: palm branches are even used to make ashes for Ash Wednesday.

questions.q: What does the Paschal candle stand for?
choices: The light of the risen Christ
questions.why: In the video: the Paschal candle symbolized the light of the risen Christ.

questions.q: On Holy Saturday night, the new ____ is blessed.
questions.why: In the video: celebrations included the blessing of the new fire and the lighting of lamps and candles.

questions.q: Who was baptized at the Easter Vigil?
questions.why: In the video: the night of the Easter Vigil was for the baptism of catechumens.

questions.q: What is the Resurrection?
questions.why: In the video: the Resurrection is when Jesus rose from the dead after being crucified.

questions.q: Jesus rose from the dead ____ days after he died.
questions.why: In the video: this miracle happened three days after his death.

questions.q: Who saw Jesus at the tomb?
questions.why: In the video: many saw Jesus after he rose, including Mary Magdalene and other women at the tomb.

questions.q: Match each Gospel writer.
questions.why: In the video: the Gospels written by Matthew, Mark, Luke and John tell the story of the resurrection.

questions.q: Why did people start coloring Easter eggs?
choices: Eggs weren't eaten in Lent, so they saved them for Easter
questions.why: In the video: eggs were not allowed during Lent, so people saved them and colored them red for Easter joy.

questions.q: What is lit from the Easter fire?
questions.why: In the video: the fire is lit by the priest and used to light the Paschal candle.

questions.q: The Easter season lasts from Easter until ____.
questions.why: In the video: the Easter season starts on Easter and ends on Pentecost.

questions.q: When does the Easter Vigil Mass start?
choices: At night, after the sun goes down
questions.why: In the video: the Easter Vigil starts late at night after the sun goes down.

questions.q: Which day of the week is Easter always on?
questions.why: In the video: it was decided that Easter would always be on a Sunday.

questions.q: Easter is the first Sunday after the first full ____ after March 21.
questions.why: In the video: Easter is on the first Sunday after the first full moon following March 21st.

questions.q: Why did the Church want one date for Easter?
questions.why: In the video: the most important thing was that the Church wanted everyone to celebrate Easter together.

questions.q: How long is the Easter season?
questions.why: In the video: Paschaltide lasts from Easter Sunday until Pentecost.

questions.q: What color does the priest wear in the Easter season?
questions.why: In the video: the season is marked by white vestments, the Gloria and the Alleluia.

questions.q: In the Easter season we sing “____!” again.
questions.why: In the video: Paschaltide is marked by saying the Alleluia.

questions.q: How often does the Church encourage us to receive Communion?
choices: Sundays and feast days, even daily
questions.why: In the video, quoting Catechism 1389: receive the Eucharist on Sundays and feast days, or more often still, even daily.

questions.q: Where was Blessed Stepinac the Archbishop?
questions.why: In the video: Aloysius Stepinac was the Archbishop of Zagreb, in Croatia.

questions.q: During the war, what did he do for people in danger?
questions.why: In the video: he protected people who were in danger, even people of other religions.

questions.q: Pope Pius XII made him a ____.
questions.why: In the video: in 1952 Pope Pius XII recognized his devotion and made him a cardinal.

questions.q: What job do cherubim have in the Bible?
questions.why: In the video: they have a special job: they guard important places, like the Garden of Eden.

questions.q: Cherubim guarded the Garden of ____.
questions.why: In the video: in the Bible, cherubim protected the Garden of Eden.

questions.q: Where were two cherubim made in gold?
choices: On the Ark of the Covenant
questions.why: In the video: cherubim figures were on the mercy seat of the Ark and in the Holy of Holies.

questions.q: What are evil angels?
questions.why: In the video: these angels were once good, but they turned against God.

questions.q: Which archangel fought the dragon?
questions.why: In the video: the devil, shown as a dragon, fought against Archangel Michael.

questions.q: Who helps us choose good?
questions.why: In the video: we always have help from Jesus Christ and our guardian angel to do good things.

questions.q: How many choirs (groups) of angels are there?
questions.why: In the video: Saint Gregory the Great says there are nine groups of angels.

questions.q: Which of these is a choir of angels?
questions.why: In the video: the nine are angels, archangels, virtues, powers, principalities, dominions, thrones, cherubim and seraphim.

questions.q: Angels are ____ and guardians created by God.
questions.why: In the video: angels are spiritual beings, messengers and guardians created by God.

questions.q: What did Gabriel tell the Virgin Mary?
choices: She would be the mother of Jesus
questions.why: In the video: Gabriel was the angel of the Annunciation, who told the Virgin Mary about the birth of Christ.

questions.q: Gabriel told Zechariah about the birth of John the ____.
questions.why: In the video: in the Gospels, Gabriel told Zechariah about the birth of John the Baptist.

questions.q: Gabriel is known as the angel of God's…
questions.why: In the video: Gabriel is known as the angel of God's power and strength.

questions.q: Saint Raphael is known for…
questions.why: In the video: Raphael is an angel who is good at healing people.

questions.q: Raphael helped a boy named ____ on a journey.
questions.why: In the video: he helped a boy named Tobias on a journey and protected him from many dangers.

questions.q: The Bible names three angels. Match them.
questions.why: In the video: the Bible names only three angels: Michael, Gabriel and Raphael. Raphael healed the blindness in Tobias' family.

questions.q: What does the name Michael mean?
questions.why: In the video: the name Michael means “Who is like God?”

questions.q: Who did Michael and the good angels fight?
questions.why: In the video: in a big battle in heaven, Michael and the good angels fought against the devil and his followers.

questions.q: Saint Michael helps and ____ people.
questions.why: In the video: Saint Michael's main job is to help and protect people and to fight against Satan.

questions.q: Do angels have bodies like ours?
questions.why: In the video, from Catechism 328–330: angels are helpers from heaven who don't have physical bodies.

questions.q: Angels are God's ____.
questions.why: In the video: angels are God's messengers, like at the Annunciation and at Christ's birth.

questions.q: Which angel told Mary she would have baby Jesus?
questions.why: In the video: the angel Gabriel told Mary she would have a baby who would be the Savior of the world.

questions.q: Advent gets us ready for…
questions.why: In the video: Advent is the season of the four Sundays leading up to Christmas.

questions.q: How many Sundays are in Advent?
questions.why: In the video: Advent is the four Sundays and weekdays before Christmas.

questions.q: In Advent the priest usually wears ____.
questions.why: In the video: the priest usually wears violet or purple vestments in Advent.

questions.q: “Advent” comes from a Latin word that means “to ____”.
questions.why: In the video: Advent, from Advenire in Latin, means to come to.

questions.q: How many candles are on an Advent wreath?
questions.why: In the video: the wreath has four candles for the four weeks of Advent.

questions.q: Why is the wreath round and evergreen?
questions.why: In the video: the round shape of evergreen is a reminder that God's love never ends.

questions.q: Most of the candles are purple, and one is ____.
questions.why: In the video: usually three candles are purple and one is rose.

questions.q: Where did the Advent wreath come from?
questions.why: In the video: the Advent wreath comes from Germany.

questions.q: Which Sunday of Advent is Gaudete Sunday?
questions.why: In the video: the third Sunday of Advent is known as Gaudete.

questions.q: “Gaudete” means ____!
questions.why: In the video: Gaudete means rejoice.

questions.q: Match each joyful Sunday to its season.
questions.why: In the video: Gaudete Sunday is much like Laetare Sunday, which is in the middle of Lent. On both the priest may wear rose.

questions.q: What hangs on a Jesse tree?
questions.why: In the video: Jesse trees have ornaments of the events around Jesus' birth and the Old Testament prophecies.

questions.q: When do families make a Jesse tree?
questions.why: In the video: many parishes and families make Jesse trees during Advent.

questions.q: A Jesse tree helps us get ready for ____.
questions.why: In the video: it's a way to reflect on these events while preparing for the celebration of Christmas.

questions.q: What do the lights on a Christmas tree stand for?
choices: Christ, the light of the world
questions.why: In the video: the Christmas light or candle symbolized Christ, the light of the world.

questions.q: Which saint is in the legend of the first Christmas tree?
questions.why: In the video: the German legend is about Saint Boniface, an English bishop who preached in Germany.

questions.q: The Christmas tree can stay up until the feast of ____.
questions.why: In the video: the tree is set up just before Christmas and may stay until the solemnity of Epiphany.

questions.q: Who made the first nativity scene?
questions.why: In the video: the custom owes its origin to Saint Francis of Assisi, on Christmas Eve in 1223.

questions.q: Who is in a nativity scene?
questions.why: In the video: it includes Mary, Joseph and the baby Jesus, the shepherds, the wise men and animals.

questions.q: Saint Francis brought hay and an ____ to the manger.
questions.why: In the video: he prepared a manger and brought hay and an ox.

questions.q: When is Saint Valentine's feast day?
questions.why: In the video: both Saint Valentines were martyrs whose feast is celebrated on February 14th.

questions.q: What was the first Saint Valentine?
questions.why: In the video: the first Saint Valentine was a priest who lived in Rome in the 3rd century.

questions.q: Valentine would not stop being a ____, even when the emperor told him to.
questions.why: In the video: told to renounce the Christian God, he said, “No, never.”

questions.q: Mother Cabrini was the first saint from which country?
questions.why: In the video: Mother Cabrini was our first United States saint.

questions.q: Where did the Pope send her instead of China?
questions.why: In the video: Pope Leo XIII told her, “Not China, but the United States.”

questions.q: She started many hospitals, homes and ____ for people in need.
questions.why: In the video: she founded 67 hospitals, homes and institutions, and she started as a school teacher.

questions.q: Who did she help in America?
questions.why: In the video: thousands of Italians were coming to America and needed help in a strange country.

questions.q: When are statues covered in church?
questions.why: In the video: crosses and images are covered from the fifth Sunday of Lent.

questions.q: Why do we veil them?
choices: To help us get ready for Easter
questions.why: In the video: veiling shows it's a special time of preparing for Easter, like a surprise gift we can't wait to open.

questions.q: Put the three days of the Triduum in order.
questions.why: In the video: these weeks get us ready for the Triduum: Holy Thursday, Good Friday and Holy Saturday.

questions.q: Who did Father Coindre want to help?
questions.why: In the video: in France there were many homeless boys who were always in trouble, and he took them in.

questions.q: What did he teach the boys?
choices: A trade, so they'd stay busy
questions.why: In the video: he hired men to teach the boys the silk weavers' trade, to keep them busy and out of trouble.

questions.q: The new order was named the Brothers of the Sacred ____.
questions.why: In the video: “your name will be Brothers of the Sacred Heart.”

questions.q: How many wings did the seraphim have in Isaiah's vision?
questions.why: In the video: in Isaiah chapter 6, he saw angels called seraphim who served God, and they had six wings.

questions.q: The seraphim sang: “Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of ____.”
questions.why: In the video: they called out, “Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of hosts. All the earth is full of his glory.”

questions.q: What did a seraph touch Isaiah's lips with?
questions.why: In the video: one of the angels touched Isaiah's lips with a lump of hot coal.

questions.q: If we get distracted while praying, what do we do?
choices: Turn our thoughts back to God
questions.why: In the video: we can continue praying once we've focused our attention back on God.

questions.q: Match each kind of prayer.
questions.why: In the video: vocal prayer is praying out loud, and mental prayer is thinking about God without set words.

questions.q: Jesus gave us the Our ____ to pray.
questions.why: In the video: we can say prayers people have already written, like how Jesus gave us the Our Father.

questions.q: Who answers our prayers?
questions.why: In the video: we can only pray to God, and only God can answer our prayers.

questions.q: Can we ask the saints to pray for us?
choices: Yes, they pray to God with us
questions.why: In the video: we can ask for the help of friends, family and the saints, who pray to God with us.

questions.q: Praying for other people is called ____ prayer.
questions.why: In the video: intercessory prayer is when we pray for other people.

questions.q: In the legend, what did Rosalind give the children at the Easter party?
questions.why: In the video: she painted the eggs with bright flowers and verses for the Easter party.

questions.q: Who took them in when they had no home?
choices: A kind miller and his wife
questions.why: In the video: the miller and his wife gladly gave them a home.

questions.q: Put the story in order.
items: A pilgrim reads a painted egg
questions.why: In the video: they fled to the miller's home, Rosalind painted eggs for Easter, a pilgrim saw one, and it was Arno, who found them.

questions.q: When do Catholics make the Sign of the Cross?
questions.why: In the video: Catholics make the sign of the cross when they begin their prayers.

questions.q: “In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy ____.”
questions.why: In the video: we trace the cross while saying, in the name of the Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Long ago, when did Christians make the sign of the cross?
questions.why: In the video: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem said to make it over the bread we eat, when traveling, before sleep, in everything.

questions.q: If we don't get what we prayed for, what should we believe?
choices: God has a bigger plan for us
questions.why: In the video: when we don't get what we ask for, believe that God has a bigger plan than we can imagine.

questions.q: Why might God not give us something we asked for?
choices: It wouldn't be good for us
questions.why: In the video: sometimes we pray for the wrong things, and God knows what's best for us (James 4:3).

questions.q: God can answer prayers through family, friends and natural ____.
questions.why: In the video: sometimes God grants our prayers by using natural events, family and friends.

questions.q: To pray well, we need…
questions.why: In the video: to pray effectively, we need to have faith and trust in God.

questions.q: In Jesus' story, whose prayer pleased God?
questions.why: In the video: the story of the Pharisee and the tax collector (Luke 18) shows we must pray humbly.

questions.q: When we pray we should be ____, not demanding.
questions.why: In the video: for prayer to work, it's important to be humble. Demanding things from God is not prayer.

questions.q: What was Saint Gabriel's name before he became a religious brother?
questions.why: In the video: his name was Francis Possenti, from Assisi, Italy.

questions.q: As a boy, what was Francis known for?
questions.why: In the video: as a young boy, Francis was known for his generosity. He was always giving something to the poor.

questions.q: Francis said the most brilliant career is to give your life completely to ____.
questions.why: In the video: “I will never have any peace until I give my life completely to God. That is the most brilliant career any man can have.”

questions.q: Why do we kneel, bow or fold our hands when we pray?
choices: To show love and respect for God
questions.why: In the video: our posture while praying shows our respect and devotion to God.

questions.q: Early Christians prayed standing with arms stretched out, like Jesus on the ____.
questions.why: In the video: the orans posture is standing with hands stretched out like Jesus did on the cross.

questions.q: Where should we use prayer postures?
questions.why: In the video: in public, such as during Mass, and also in private prayer, like morning and night prayers.

questions.q: How does prayer help us?
questions.why: In the video: we need prayer because it helps us resist temptation and receive God's grace.

questions.q: How often does the Bible tell us to pray?
questions.why: In the video: the Bible tells us to pray constantly, whenever we need to, which is often.

questions.q: Prayer helps us grow in our ____.
questions.why: In the video: prayer helps us receive God's grace and grow in our faith.

questions.q: What is vocal prayer?
questions.why: In the video: vocal prayer involves speaking out loud or thinking words while praying.

questions.q: Which is a vocal prayer?
questions.why: In the video: examples of vocal prayer are the Lord's Prayer and the Psalms, hymns and litanies.

questions.q: Match each kind of prayer.
questions.why: In the video: prayer done alone is private prayer; with others, it's public prayer.

questions.q: What is mental prayer?
questions.why: In the video: meditation, or mental prayer, is when we reflect deeply on God's truths and mysteries.

questions.q: Another word for mental prayer is ____.
questions.why: In the video: meditation, also known as mental prayer, is a beautiful practice in the Catholic faith.

questions.q: Who in the Gospels is often shown praying quietly?
questions.why: In the video: in the New Testament, Jesus is often shown meditating in the Gospels.

questions.q: Which is a public prayer of the whole Church?
questions.why: In the video: every Mass is a public prayer, and so are sacraments like baptism and matrimony.

questions.q: Match each prayer.
questions.why: In the video: public prayer is offered officially, like the Mass; private prayer is our own prayer, alone or with others.

questions.q: Praying together helps us connect with other ____.
questions.why: In the video: public prayer is a way to connect with other Catholics.

questions.q: Who does the Byzantine Catholic Church trace its start to?
questions.why: In the video: the Byzantine Catholic Church traces its foundation back to the 12 apostles.

questions.q: The disciples were first called Christians in ____.
questions.why: In the video: Antioch is where the disciples were first called Christians.

questions.q: Match each tradition to its language.
questions.why: In the video: two traditions grew from the earliest days: the Eastern, or Greek, and the Western, or Latin.

questions.q: What is another name for Pascha?
questions.why: In the video: Pascha is the feast of the Resurrection, also commonly known as Easter.

questions.q: Pascha means God ____.
questions.why: In the video: the word Pascha comes from the Exodus, when God saved his people from Egypt. It means God saves.

questions.q: Someone says “Christ is risen!” What do you answer?
questions.why: In the video: people greet each other with “Christ is risen,” and you answer, “Indeed, he is risen.”

questions.q: Where was Pope Francis from?
questions.why: In the video: Pope Francis was born Jorge Mario Bergoglio in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

questions.q: Why did he choose the name Francis?
choices: For Saint Francis, who loved nature and the poor
He picked it from a hat
questions.why: In the video: he chose Francis because Saint Francis of Assisi was known for his love of nature and helping the poor.

questions.q: Put his life in order.
questions.why: In the video: priest in the Jesuit order, Archbishop of Buenos Aires in 1998, cardinal in 2001, and Pope in 2013.

questions.q: He was the first Pope from South ____.
questions.why: In the video: Pope Francis was the first pope from South America, and the first who was a Jesuit.

questions.q: Who chooses the new Pope?
questions.why: In the video: cardinals travel to Vatican City from all over the world to choose the new Pope.

questions.q: In Latin, “conclave” means locked with a ____.
questions.why: In the video: in Latin, conclave means locked with a key.

questions.q: Where do the cardinals vote?
questions.why: In the video: they go into a famous room called the Sistine Chapel, painted by Michelangelo.

questions.q: Who was the first Pope?
questions.why: In the video: Jesus appointed Saint Peter as the first Pope, and there has been an unbroken line since.

questions.q: Where was Pope Leo XIV born?
questions.why: In the video: Robert Francis Prevost was born in Chicago in 1955.

questions.q: Where did he spend many years as a missionary?
questions.why: In the video: he joined the mission to Peru and spent most of his time there, later becoming a bishop there.

questions.q: He is the first Pope from North ____.
questions.why: In the video: he is the first North American pope.

questions.q: Which religious order did he join?
questions.why: In the video: he became a priest in the Order of Saint Augustine.

questions.q: Where was Saint Vladimir the Grand Prince?
questions.why: In the video: Vladimir the Great was Grand Prince of Kyiv from 978 until his death in 1015.

questions.q: After he became a Christian, what did he do?
choices: Built churches and gave to the poor
questions.why: In the video: he became a Christian and Christianized his country by building churches and giving to the poor.

questions.q: Of all the religions he heard about, Vladimir liked ____ best.
questions.why: In the video: missionaries from many religions came, but he wasn't impressed by any of them except Christianity.
